content: {"like":["These episodes represent a departure from the rather mundane scripts of the last several years.","By contrast, the Morse episodes were diverse and only a few dealt with the colleges directly.","there's a certain thematic diversity that's been lacking in previous seasons.","solidified Lewis as a soon to be happy pensioner.","Lewis Season 6 stands on its own as a fitting denouement to a storyline and title character many have known for over 25 years.","Have your 'happy life' Robbie, we'll miss you."],"dislike":["episodes soon became repetitive, at times pretentious, and certainly not worthy of the sequel status PBS had appended to it.","Lewis producers turned the time honored Oxford social tension of 'town and gown' into all gown and no town.","inability of the writers to develop Lewis into a dominant lead character limited the episodes to be a pleasant but shallow police procedural rather than the personality driven drama of its predecessor.","writing is still weak and too much time is wasted showing Lewis and Hathaway strolling across the same college courtyards they seem to cover in every film.","didn't resolve the 'is he or isn't he gay' tease on Hathaway."]}
